review_notes: I read the whole file and the sibling uses in UnitriangularLowerCentralSeries.lean and in the AlgebraicGroupsTest files. I also read GeneralLinearGroups/Elementary.lean, where the underlying `elementaryUnit_val` is already `@[simp]`. The file has no simp attributes at all. I found one missing-simp-lemma issue: `elementary_coe`. I did not recommend simp on `elementary_commutator`, because its LHS needs side hypotheses and explicit index and order proofs, and its uses are `simpa only` with an explicit `hroot`. I also did not recommend simp on `elementary_gl` in addition to `elementary_coe`. I expect `elementary_gl` to compete with `elementary_coe`, because simp rewrites the inner `.1` first. I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed attribute compiles or that existing `simp [elementary_coe]` calls still close their goals.

findings.problem: `elementary_coe` is the canonical entry-level unfolding of `elementary`, which is a `def` built by tactic. It has no `@[simp]` attribute. Its upstream analogue `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.elementaryUnit_val` is `@[simp]`, so the unitriangular wrapper breaks the simp chain. Without the attribute, `simp` cannot see through `elementary` to `1 + Matrix.single i j a` and `Matrix.single_apply`/`Matrix.add_apply` never fire. Every caller must name `elementary_coe` by hand, or use `rw`, or `change` first. The call at line 110 of this file, `simp [elementary_coe, Matrix.add_apply, hzero] at hentry`, does this. So do `simp [shear, Matrix.UnitriangularGroup.elementary_coe, Matrix.add_apply]` in the UpperTriangularSchemeProduct test and `rw [elementary_coe]` at two places in UnitriangularLowerCentralSeries.lean. The RHS is a strictly more primitive expression, so there is no loop risk. The identity is also stated by `rfl` and is not trivial in a bad direction. It is the only way to compute matrix entries of `elementary`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`, as for `elementaryUnit_val`. Do not also tag `elementary_gl`. Simp rewrites the inner `(elementary ..).1` first, so the two lemmas would compete. Keep `elementary_gl` as a plain lemma. Then the explicit `elementary_coe` arguments in the `simp [...]` calls (line 110 and the tests) can be dropped, and the `rw [elementary_coe]` calls can become `simp`.
findings.benefit: Entry computations on `elementary` then normalise to `1 + Matrix.single i j a` and further to `Matrix.single_apply`/`Matrix.one_apply` by default. Downstream files stop repeating `elementary_coe` in every simp set. Users who forget it no longer get stuck on an opaque `elementary` term.
